According to Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman, Apple is making significant changes to its retail stores to pave the way for an upcoming home product line. Apple will at least unveil a brand-new HomePod mini and Apple TV 4K this autumn, though the changes appear to indicate a third, even more important product will also debut alongside them.

Apple has accumulated a large backlog of home products waiting to launch, mainly because the comprehensive Siri upgrade has been delayed multiple times. Now that Siri integration is finally complete, a product line that hasn't been updated in years is finally set to see the light of day.

That said, earlier reports indicated Apple would first release new versions of the HomePod mini and Apple TV 4K, while its first smart home hub (also known as a HomePod or HomePad with display) might not arrive until later.

However, according to the latest news, this smart home hub could launch simultaneously with the new Apple TV and HomePod mini, and the current preparations at retail stores seem to confirm this. Quoting from the Power On newsletter:

Of course, everything will only be confirmed at Apple's September event. Based on current reports, the all-new smart home hub should make its debut very soon, alongside the new Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini with Siri AI support.

Summary

Based on rumors, Apple's smart home hub will feature a 7-inch square display and come in two versions: one with built-in speakers, and another with magnets on the back for wall mounting. The product will run on a brand-new operating system with a home screen supporting Widgets, usable for FaceTime calls, and serving as the hub for all smart home accessories and Siri. On the hardware side, it will be powered by an A18 chip.

Another new rumor about Apple's home product line is that the next-generation Apple TV 4K might come with a new Siri Remote, though specific changes remain unclear.

Are you interested in the new home products? Which one are you most looking forward to? Let us know in the comments.
